summary.headline: IndiGo swung to a net loss of INR 2.4 billion in Q1 FY27 as fuel CASK rose ~80% YoY, despite yield growth of 21.3%.
summary.overview: IndiGo reported total income of INR 256 billion (up ~19% YoY), with EBITDAR of INR 38.3 billion at a 15.6% margin versus 28% a year earlier. Net loss was INR 2.4 billion against a profit of INR 21.8 billion in Q1 FY26; ex-currency the loss was about INR 56 million. Yield rose 21.3% and load factor fell 1.3 points to about 83%, but fuel cost rose sharply on Middle East-linked jet fuel prices and the rupee's depreciation of more than 11%. For Q2 FY27 management guided flattish capacity and PRASK growth above 25%, while holding the single-digit FY27 ASK guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 57.4 billion, 28% margin in Q1 FY26
vs profit of INR 21.8 billion in Q1 FY26; ex-currency loss ~INR 56 million

financial_highlights.value: INR 529 billion (free INR 390 billion, restricted INR 139 billion)

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic fuel charged on a government/OMC-capped formula (25% cap on March reference price) from 1 April to 8 June; market-linked from 9 June. May was the best month ever for IndiGo domestic, with over 10 million domestic passengers.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Fuel always billed at market rates, so international fuel cost rose faster than domestic. International capacity largely recovered in June; the Middle East was at around 90-95% of pre-war departures at end-June (about 150 daily before the war, 20-30 at the trough).

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 capacity expected flattish YoY, driven by route rationalisation and temporary international suspensions (e.g., Langkawi, Ho Chi Minh City, Hong Kong, Shanghai; expected to restart in October).
Q2 FY27 PRASK expected to grow more than 25% YoY; loads expected flattish to slightly down, similar to Q1.
FY27 ASK growth guidance held in single digits; FY28-FY30 capacity growth guided at early double digits to mid-teens; 300 billion-rupee capacity figure cited for FY30 at the analyst meet.
FY27 CASK ex-fuel ex-forex expected at the higher end of single digits, possibly lower end of early double digits.
International share of ASK targeted at around 40% by 2030 (about 33% currently).
No guidance given on RASK-CASK spread; damp-lease decision deferred to Q3 FY27 depending on Middle East and fuel trends.
capex_capacity: Fleet at quarter end: 432 aircraft; inducted 13 aircraft from original orderbook (via GIFT City entity) and redelivered 9 orderbook aircraft and 13 damp-leased aircraft.
Q1 capacity growth ~3% YoY, broadly in line with guidance; Q1 was Middle East-driven, Q2 reduction is off-season related.
Older CEO-technology aircraft parked where commercially appropriate; prioritising fuel-efficient aircraft.
Signed MoU with CFM International for over 1,000 LEAP-1A engines for future deliveries, including engine MRO and long-term material services.
Bought 4 engines via GIFT City entity; partial payment for land for unified campus.
Started flights to Jamnagar; first airline to operate from Jewar airport (Noida).
demand_pricing: Pricing actions drove yield up ~21%; management says price discipline is holding in Q2 and yields are tapering upward.
April demand hit by disruption and recalibration; May was the strongest month for the domestic industry; June yields held up while international was managed selectively.

Fuel: Singapore jet fuel up nearly 120% (Brent up ~50% YoY on average). ATF in June reportedly fell to about INR 110-115/litre at the blended level before rebounding; management estimated the quarter's blended effective rate around INR 140-150/litre.
Rupee depreciated more than 11%, inflating dollar costs (leases, maintenance, supplementary rentals).
Lite Fare (no check-in bag, add-on purchasing) launched; Accor ALL loyalty platform went live; SITA OptiClimb fuel-optimisation tested.

qa_highlights.question: Impact on load factors from higher yields, and is capacity rationalisation driven by this?
qa_highlights.answer: Load factor fell only 1.3 points in Q1; Q2 loads expected flattish to slightly down as capacity is cut, with pricing discipline holding.

qa_highlights.question: Has fuel consumption per ASK changed, and what was the effective fuel rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumption per ASK unchanged; only the rate moved. Management described the April-8 June domestic cap (25% on a March reference), VAT/excise, and market-priced international and private supply, with an average around INR 140-150/litre.

qa_highlights.question: Will the fuel CASK increase of ~63% QoQ reconcile with the OMC price-cap releases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to March being an elevated base, the capped domestic formula plus taxes, market-priced international fuel, and private suppliers pricing at market.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 capacity guidance changing?
qa_highlights.answer: No change: FY27 ASK growth still single digits. Mid-teens growth is still held for FY28-FY30 (described as early double digits to mid-teens).

qa_highlights.question: Any risk of having to compensate OMCs for April-May fuel support?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the April-8 June bills were settled on the agreed formula, and it expects no extra burden because fares were passed through.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FX loss and supplementary rental trends?
qa_highlights.answer: FX mark-to-market loss was about INR 80 million; the rupee moved only about 10 paise over the quarter, on a USD exposure of about USD 8-9 billion. Supplementary rentals rose on currency and escalation, with a Q4 release base effect.

qa_highlights.question: Will yields hold after fuel normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is price-led for now; after fuel moderates, it expects to return to volume-led growth and hold prices, with mid-teens growth post FY27.

risks_watch: Fuel volatility: forward curves moved up again in July with Brent back above USD 90; a Hormuz disruption could bring Q1-like fuel levels.
Middle East airspace: capacity at around 90% of pre-war levels, but the crisis has flared again; management is assessing further restoration.
Ability to sustain yields beyond Q2 as capacity returns for the Q3 peak season, and the damp-lease decision in Q3.
Cost pressure: CASK ex-fuel up ~11% YoY; deferred senior management increments to be reassessed in six months; gratuity-related exceptional costs expected in Q3 and Q4.
Reported news on airport operators entering airlines: management said it is watching developments and gave no decision.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and pricing near term, but cautious and evasive on margin: management declined to give a spread or fuel-pass-through target and repeatedly described the environment as too volatile to guide on profitability.
key_quotes: As we enter a seasonally softer demand period and continue to manage fuel and airspace volatility, we are adopting a prudent and measured approach to capacity.
So, there's no kind of a target, but we just want it to be a healthy kind of a spread.
We are holding to the guidance that we gave at the analyst meet.

growth.why: Q2 FY27 capacity guided flattish YoY and PRASK >25%, FY27 ASK growth held single-digit, FY28-FY30 capacity growth mid-teens with a 1,000+ LEAP-1A engine MoU and fleet deliveries behind it, but near-term growth is largely pricing-driven and the Q2 capacity is flat.
